findings.summary: The canary scans passed on empty, truncated or partial store answers, so the gate could report no canary without having seen the run's data (fixed in a8baaad).
Prometheus exemplars were searched for the two time-to-queue histograms only, while the contract forbids a canary in any exemplar (fixed in a8baaad).
Three of the four canary searches and the link's trace-id comparison had no test that could fail (fixed in a8baaad).
The account-number canary is sent only in a refused request, and the real ingest key and token of accepted requests are not searched for.
The Tempo canary scan fails closed at 50 listed traces, so a busier stack would fail with cannot tell.
The stop trap in check.sh prints the last 40 log lines of every service unredacted; the contract canaries are synthetic, so no real secret is at risk.
No test covers check.sh's exit-code logic, which was checked by reading and simulation only.
The README's probe paragraph does not mention the probe's new --trace-id option.
The fix round edited the test file's fake store once with an inline replace script instead of the edit tool.
